title.en: Food, textiles and an epic spread

text.en:
At Meena's school fair each child wore a different dress and brought a different dish.
"One country, many styles," said the teacher.

India's food changes with place and climate: rice in the south, wheat in the north, fish by the coast. Yet sharing meals unites us.
Textiles differ too: silk from Kanchipuram, cotton from Bengal, bandhani from Gujarat, and each region has its dress such as sari, dhoti, kurta and lungi.
The Ramayana and Mahabharata spread across India and South-East Asia in many versions, showing shared stories.
